Note::TexAccessor::strip_metadata¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_metadata() const

Remove Front-Matter Declarations¶

strip_metadata() removes complete \title{...}, \author{...}, \date{...}, and \thanks{...} calls, plus the bare \maketitle command. It is intended for source that should retain its document body while discarding title-page identity and presentation directives. It is narrower than strip_preamble(): packages, document-class declarations, and document boundaries remain untouched.

The four argument-taking commands are removed only when their required braced body is complete. Bodies may contain nested balanced braces. Command matching is exact and case-sensitive; escaped spellings, longer names such as \titlecase, starred forms, and malformed calls survive. \maketitle is a complete bare command and therefore needs no group. Whitespace around removed regions is collapsed to one ASCII space and each cell is trimmed.

The method allocates a new Text Note and preserves rank, shape, and lane count. An all-metadata cell becomes an empty string. It is idempotent, propagates undefined state, and rejects defined non-Text input. The lexical scan is linear in source bytes and uses stack depth proportional to nested group depth.

Example 1: Complete Metadata And Nested Bodies¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \title{Nested {title}} \author {Ada} \maketitle B)",
    R"(\date{2026} x \thanks{Supported by {Lab}} y)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_metadata() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["A B", "x y"]

Example 2: Escaped, Longer, And Incomplete Forms Survive¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    R"(\\date{x} \titlecase{y} \thanks{broken})");
std::cout << source.tex().strip_metadata() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"\\\\date{x} \\titlecase{y} \\thanks{broken"

Example 3: Empty Results Retain Their Matrix Position¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\title{A})", "plain",
                             R"(x \author{B} y)", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().strip_metadata() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["", "plain"],
  ["x y", ""]
]

Example 4: Idempotence And Type Boundaries¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note(R"(A \title{x} B)")
                      .tex().strip_metadata();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent="
          << ((once == once.tex().strip_metadata()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_metadata().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_metadata();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
Int64: rejected
